knowledge.name: Answers from your knowledge
knowledge.what: Ada searches your knowledge base and writes the reply from the articles it finds, so the answer matches your own policy.
knowledge.why: Update one article and every future answer on that topic changes with it.
knowledge.try: Tighten or add an article for the topics where customers ask the most.

playbook.name: Step-by-step guidance
playbook.what: A playbook is a set of instructions for one task, such as a refund or a rebooking. Ada follows it step by step and adapts to what the customer says.
playbook.why: The customer is walked to an outcome in the chat, not sent a link to read.
playbook.try: Turn your most common how-to question into a playbook.

action.name: Doing things in your systems
action.what: An action lets Ada look something up or change it in your order, booking or account system during the chat, and use the result in its reply.
action.why: The customer gets an answer about their own order, not a generic one.
action.try: Connect the one lookup this topic needs most.

handoff.name: Handing off with context
handoff.what: When a person needs to step in, Ada passes the conversation across with what it has already collected.
handoff.why: Your team starts from the answer, not from asking the customer to repeat themselves.
handoff.try: Review what Ada collects before a handoff, and add anything your team always asks next.

coaching.name: Coaching
coaching.what: You review a past conversation and tell Ada what it should have done. Ada applies that in similar situations from then on.
coaching.why: One correction improves the whole pattern, with no rewrite of a playbook.
coaching.try: Review five conversations from one topic and coach the ones that missed.

guidance.name: Standing instructions
guidance.what: Short rules that apply to every conversation, such as tone, or things Ada should never promise.
guidance.why: Every reply stays consistent with how your brand speaks.
guidance.try: Write down the three things your best agents always do and check that Ada does them.

image.name: Reading photos and screenshots
image.what: When a customer sends a picture on messaging or email, Ada reads what it shows, including visible text, and uses that in the conversation.
image.why: The customer skips typing out an order number or describing damage.
image.try: Pick one topic where a photo saves the customer three questions.

topics.name: Topics
topics.what: Ada sorts every conversation into a topic on its own, so you can see what customers ask and how each topic resolves.
topics.why: You find the biggest opportunity by volume, not by guessing.
topics.try: Sort topics by volume, then look at the ones with the lowest resolution.

custom-metric.name: Your own quality measures
custom-metric.what: A custom metric scores each conversation against a standard you set, such as whether the agent confirmed the refund amount.
custom-metric.why: You track what matters to your business, not only generic scores.
custom-metric.try: Add one measure for the outcome you most want to improve.

code-tool.name: Small pieces of logic
code-tool.what: A code tool is a short routine Ada runs mid-chat to work something out, such as a date, a total, or a reshaped answer from your system.
code-tool.why: Rules that are easy to state but hard to write in prose are applied the same way every time.
code-tool.try: List the sums and date rules your team does by hand during these chats.
